- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.5) or negative (≤-0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect or underreact — adjust forecast by 2–5% in direction of sentiment, especially if price is trending sharply.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or reversal, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >10% from recent high), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 7–10 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.25), model tends to underestimate volatility — increase forecast variance by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat — if model is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows early drop after forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% in first 3 days after peak, especially if sentiment is negative.
- For sentiment-heavy periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.5+ or -0.5-), model tends to lag — add 1–2% lag correction to forecast if price is trending downward or upward, respectively.
